Chronic rhinosinusitis remains a plausible diagnosis despite the absence of some typical symptoms like nasal congestion, as it might primarily present with pain in the facial and head regions due to inflammation of the sinuses. The absence of more specific symptoms pointing to the other diseases, and given the chronic nature and localization of the pain, makes this a reasonable consideration.
